entries.appliesTo: Idaho local school districts and public charter schools; the state department of education (statewide framework, standards, guidance)

dutySources.risk-program: § 33-7004 — 'Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence by students and employees in school buildings, on school grounds, during school activities, and on school-issued devices.'

sources.policyRequired: § 33-7004 — 'Each local school district and public charter school shall adopt a policy governing the use of generative artificial intelligence'

flags: CODING.md rule 6 cites ID S 1227 as an example of a chatbot-safeguards bill filed under 'AI in Education', but the enacted text (new Chapter 70, Title 33 — 'GENERATIVE ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EDUCATION') contains no chatbot or companion-AI provisions; coded education-k12 from the text (possible confusion with ID S 1297 'Conversational AI Safety Act').

§ 33-7007(1) imposes a duty directly on private vendors — 'Vendors shall disclose whether products utilize machine learning, predictive analytics, or generative AI and shall provide assurances regarding data protection, algorithmic transparency, and responsible use' — which arguably triggers the company mixing rule for category and fits no listed duty key; left in flags rather than coded.

State department of education (not schools) is bound to: develop a statewide generative AI in education framework subject to state board approval (§ 33-7003(1) — 'The state department of education shall develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework'), develop and recommend K-12 generative AI literacy standards, assessment guidelines, and a professional development plan (§ 33-7005 — 'shall develop and recommend to the state board of education'), and develop a parent/guardian guidance document (§ 33-7006).

curriculum and trainingRequired params not coded: § 33-7005 requires the department to 'develop and recommend' literacy standards and a professional development plan — it does not mandate that schools teach the standards or that educators complete training.
§ 33-7007(2) is permissive only: 'The state department of education may establish a list of approved generative AI tools or develop model procurement guidelines' — no procurement param coded.
No penalty, enforcement, or remedy provision anywhere in the chapter — exposure omitted per rule 3.
Emergency clause: 'this act shall be in full force and effect on and after July 1, 2026' (Section 2).
